text:
Cutter Gauthier has been the story in Anaheim for two weeks: 30 headlines, a goal streak the Avalanche finally ended in a Scott Wedgewood shutout, and a seat near the top of the Rocket Richard race. He has 15 points in his last 10 games against 11.5 our numbers expected, and Beckett Sennecke ran even hotter beside him (16 points in 10). That line is the Ducks' offense.

Now it is thinner. Sennecke is on injured reserve and Leo Carlsson left a game in Utah with an upper-body injury and is day-to-day. Losing two of your three best young forwards in the same week is the kind of thing that turns a .500 team into a seller.

The bigger worry is behind them. Lukas Dostal is at .833 over his last five starts, 8.6 goals worse than expected, and Ville Husso is at .825. As a team the Ducks have allowed about eight more goals than the chances deserved, and they get only 46% of the expected goals at 5v5 (expected goals measure the quality of chances). The finishing has been carrying a roster that is being outshot.

At 12-13-1 and 25 points, our simulations give them a 44% shot at the playoffs. What to watch: whether Gauthier keeps scoring without Sennecke, and whether either goalie gives them a week of ordinary saves.
headline: Gauthier's goals can't cover the crease
